content.text: Yu An, I've been preparing for an important restoration project recently and need to purchase a batch of antique-style handmade Xuan paper. This is a sample roll—it's light yellow in color with very fine fibers.
Jingyan, this paper looks so gentle! Just like the tea you shared before, it has a calming aura. Where are you going to purchase it?

There is a paper mill in the suburbs that has been passed down through generations, and I plan to go there to take a look. Choosing paper isn’t about price or whiteness; it’s about ‘matching’—like finding a fitting yet humble undergarment for an ancient book.
This metaphor is truly beautiful! It reminds me of our discussion about 'conversing with paper.' I've always been curious about traditional crafts—may I join you?
Of course. This journey to find paper might also help you better understand the value of 'slowness'—just as we discussed earlier, choosing paper requires patience and perception.
Great! I've recently introduced 'slow creation' in my workshop and I'm eager to experience more of this traditional form of mindfulness. Is there anything I need to prepare?

Wear shoes that don't show dirt; there might be pulp in the paper mill. Look at this picture—this rough fibrous surface is the base of handmade paper. For restoration, the paper used needs to be slightly thinner and softer than the original, with matching fibers.
I see, just like in art therapy where you 'listen' to the client's emotional undertones. What about the colors? You mentioned 'aging' treatment earlier?
Yes, the color should age naturally, not be chemically dyed. This requires time to settle, just like the 'steadiness' brought by the ink-stained old cat—it cannot be rushed.

Speaking of ink marks, creating this commemorative book has taught me to better understand the concept of 'cherishing without attachment.' This time, selecting the paper felt like a similar exercise in mindfulness.
This is the map of Zhifang Town. Let's go there this weekend. Look, there are many green areas, and the environment is very peaceful, perfect for taking our time to choose.

The sunset scenery on the map is so beautiful! It reminds me of the "Quietly Accompanying the Flow of Time" you shared. This journey together can be considered an extension of our collaboration on the "Mindfulness Guide," right?
Well, avoiding dogmatism is good. The process of selecting paper itself is a kind of sensory diary—touching, observing, and listening to the sound of the paper.
Just like the mental technique of 'unifying the mind, eyes, and hands' that you use when restoring things? I'm getting more and more excited—this is much more meaningful than simply shopping.

Yes, it's about 'harmony between things and oneself.' Yu An, thank you for taking the time to understand all of this—from emotional doodles to the journey of finding paper, our conversation has been deepening.
Jing Yan, it was you who taught me that 'stillness can give rise to wisdom.' This time, I will approach learning with an open mind, just like experiencing the 'lingering sweetness' when drinking tea.
So we'll set off on Saturday morning? The paper mill opens at nine, so we can take our time looking around and have a simple lunch nearby.
Great! I'll wear shoes that don't show dirt easily and bring a notebook—maybe I can do some quick sketches to gather material for the 'Sensory Awakening' module.
Great idea. Yu An, this trip together is not just about selecting paper, but also a continuation of our mutual nourishment—I’m really looking forward to sharing this traditional aesthetic with you.
Me too! From seeking peace of mind to exploring together, every conversation helps me accept myself more. See you on Saturday, Jingyan.
